model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for several language model variants. The x-axis represents "#Iteration" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents "Loss" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1.

Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model configuration. The purple line labeled "Vanilla" starts at approximately 3.4 at iteration 0 and decreases steeply in the early iterations, then gradually levels off, reaching approximately 2.50 by iteration 140,000. The blue line labeled "StrmLLM (n=64)" follows a similar initial steep decline but settles at a noticeably higher loss, ending at approximately 2.62 by iteration 140,000. The orange line labeled "SepLLM (n=64)" closely tracks the Vanilla line throughout training, starting near 3.4 and ending at approximately 2.52. The green line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H)" behaves very similarly to the orange line, ending at approximately 2.52 as well. The red line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" also follows a nearly identical trajectory to the Vanilla, orange, and green lines, ending at approximately 2.51–2.52. The dark blue line labeled "SepLLM (n=128)" starts similarly near 3.4 and ends at approximately 2.53, following a trajectory very close to the other SepLLM variants. All lines exhibit a rapid decrease in loss during the first approximately 20,000 iterations, after which the rate of decrease slows considerably. The StrmLLM (n=64) line remains consistently above all other lines after the initial phase, while the Vanilla and SepLLM variants cluster closely together at lower loss values. Light shaded regions around each line appear to indicate variability or confidence intervals.
